summary: Chelan County, WA: 40-ft pole L-4 lookout on Chelan Butte, dated 1936 or 1938 by source, replaced 1939, moved to the Columbia Breaks center in 1995.

facts.design: 40-ft pole tower with L-4 cab, replaced in 1939 by a 28-ft treated timber tower with L-4 cab
facts.status_note: The timber tower moved to the Columbia Breaks Fire Interpretive Center in 1995; the association lists the original tower as gone
facts.agency: U.S.Forest Service/Washington Dept. of Natural Resources

access.note: The center's lookouts are open inside only during center events or by special arrangement; the original summit is not described today

events.note: First tower, a 40-ft pole tower with an L-4 cab, per the register and FireLookout.com
1937 newspaper item quoted on Washington Lookouts: Marvin Kelly at the new station, cabin still being built
NRHP: a Civilian Conservation Corps crew led by Sim Beeson built the road to the site in 1938, so the tower and cabin could follow
The first 40-ft pole tower burned down; the year is not given
Replaced by a 28-ft treated timber tower with L-4 cab
A fire ran over the butte and burned under the tower; the Forest Service lookout stayed at his post
Listed December 27, 1990; the nomination describes the lookout at the summit on state land
Moved to the Columbia Breaks Fire Interpretive Center, a mile north of Entiat
Registered on the Former Fire Lookout Sites register August 21, 2012

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register and FireLookout.com date the first tower to 1936; the NRHP nomination says a CCC crew built the road, tower and cabin in 1938; a 1937 newspaper item describes a new station being built. The story reports all three and does not pick one.
FireLookout.com puts the butte two miles south of Chelan; a 1963 newspaper item quoted on Washington Lookouts says seven miles. The story reports both and does not pick one.

notes_for_editor: The build year is the main conflict: 1936 (register, FireLookout.com), 1938 (NRHP, which also says the road was built that year), 1937 (newspaper item, 'new look-out station'). The NRHP nomination describes the summit before the 1995 move, so it cannot describe the current exhibit. The story gives no highway route. The 1963 fire item says it burned under the tower but does not say the tower was lost. No new photos added; the register photos are on the parent record.
